chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram may not cover himself from the sun with a garment, and there is no objection if he covers part of himself with another part (of his body).

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.بَعْضَهُ بِبَعْضٍ: Part of himself with another part (referring to using hands/feet to shade the body)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on covering the head or body from the sun while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between 'covering' (istitar) and 'shading' (istilal) in Shia jurisprudence, permitting the use of one's own hand or foot to shield the head from direct sunlight without invalidating the Ihram. It reflects the scholarly consensus that the prohibition applies specifically to structured garments like turbans and cloaks, while natural shading remains permissible, a nuance critical for pilgrims seeking to balance comfort with ritual purity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Al Halby, from Al Moalla Bin Khunays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam cannot veil himself from the sun by clothes, and there is no problem if he were to veil himself with part of himself (like a hand etc.) the other parts (like face etc.)’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabiy from Mu ‘alia’ ibn Khunays who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A man in the state of Ihram must not cover himself from the sun with a cloth; but it is not harmful to cover one part by the other part of his body.’”
